messages:
alex: Heads up — observed repeated nvme errors on three us-west nodes, kernel OOMs tied to heavy IO. Pods getting evicted. Anyone picking this up?
maya: I saw the alerts earlier. iops spikes then device error logs. Nodes: gpu-uw2-32, gpu-uw2-34, gpu-uw2-37. Appears to be `nvme0n1` on all. :warning:
kevin: I'll take owner for triage. Can someone paste the SMART / nvme smart log for one node?
maya: Pasting excerpt from gpu-uw2-32 (nvme-cli):
```
$ nvme smart-log /dev/nvme0n1
critical_warning: 0
temperature: 39 C
available_spare: 100%
available_spare_threshold: 10%
percentage_used: 23
data_units_read: 1234567
data_units_written: 987654
media_errors: 12
num_err_log_entries: 240
```
Not huge but `media_errors` and `num_err_log_entries` stand out.
ops-bot: [alert] disk-error gpu-uw2-32 nvme0n1 — auto-taint applied: `storage/readonly: true`
sasha: Recommend draining 1 node at a time and running full disk checks. We should back up any local caches first (they're ephemeral but some shards are expensive to regenerate). Use `kubectl drain --ignore-daemonsets --delete-local-data` for the node after ensuring traffic shift.
danielle: We had prior cases where abrupt nvme failures caused btrfs/ext4 corruption under `/srv/cache`. Plan: unmount, run `fsck -y`, then remount. If we see inode errors do not restart the serving process until checks complete.
ryan: Agreed. Also try switching the IO scheduler to `noop` or `mq-deadline` while running heavy checks — it reduced latency spikes for us last year. Command: `echo noop > /sys/block/nvme0n1/queue/scheduler`.
alex: Proposed runbook: 1) cordon node 2) drain (one at a time) 3) snapshot relevant caches (sasha) 4) run `smartctl -a` / `nvme smart-log` 5) run `badblocks -v` then `fsck -y` if errors 6) if reallocated sectors > 100 or `media_errors` > 0x10, file RMA. Also run `fstrim` and `blkdiscard` for ephemeral volumes after cleanup.
kevin: Starting drain on gpu-uw2-32 in 5m. Will post outputs.
kevin: Drain finished. Quick `smartctl -a` shows 480 reallocated sectors and increasing `num_err_log_entries`. Here's snippet:
```
Reallocated_Sector_Ct: 480
Media_Error_Count: 12
```
Tagging for RMA criteria.
maya: If reallocated sectors are that high we should treat as failing. Also check `percentage_used` from nvme; high numbers with reallocated sectors => wear.
sasha: I'll copy live caches off node to s3-temp and invalidate local keys. Script to remove stale shards older than 6h: 
```
#!/bin/bash
find /local-nvme/cache -type f -mmin +360 -name '*.shard' -print0 | xargs -0 -n 50 rm -f
```
We should deploy that as a one-off CronJob in the maintenance window.
danielle: Reminder: `--delete-local-data` with `kubectl drain` will delete PV-backed local data — confirm volumes are ephemeral.
alex: Cost note: replacing 3 datacenter-grade NVMe ~ $5-7k each + ops time. Budget impact but RMA under warranty probable. Alternative: move some load to dedicated pools to keep latency SLOs while we RMA.
kevin: Node gpu-uw2-34 shows similar metrics; scheduling drain now. Planning to run `badblocks -s -v -n /dev/nvme0n1` and then `fsck -y` if needed.
ryan: For monitoring: let's add a fleet scan job that runs `nvme smart-log` and aggregates `media_errors`, `num_err_log_entries`, `percentage_used`, and `temperature` once per week. Add alert when `media_errors > 5` or `num_err_log_entries` delta > 50 in 24h.
maya: I'll open a monitoring PR. Also add an alert for `reallocated_sectors > 100` per device.
sasha: Ops will run cleanup cron and snapshot caches for the draining nodes.
ops-bot: Created ticket RMA-1322 for NVMe replacements (nodes: gpu-uw2-32/34/37). SLA: vendor contacted, ETA 5 business days.
alex: Good. After RMA we should run a rolling-probe across all ephemeral NVMe nodes to detect early wear. Also consider increasing eviction threshold for disk pressure to avoid OOMs from runaway IO.
kevin: Update: after `fsck` and removing corrupted cache on gpu-uw2-32, node back in rotation. SMART still unhappy — will keep cordoned until RMA.
maya: Thanks team. Postmortem + short-term ops checklist to follow. :thumbsup:
